# Forge: a 2D game engine in Rust

> Forge is a from-scratch, dependency-free 2D game engine in pure Rust by Pavan Nallamothu, built around deterministic, headless-testable simulation.

Forge is a compact but complete game engine core: an entity component system, a fixed-timestep loop, semi-implicit Euler physics, AABB and circle collision with continuous (swept) resolution, an input and event system, a scene hierarchy, and a rendering abstraction that keeps the core headless. Rendering sits behind a trait so the core never needs a screen, time advances in fixed slices so results never depend on frame rate, and randomness comes from a seeded generator inside the world state, so the whole world hashes to a single number. Given a seed and an input script the world evolves identically on every run, and it serializes, restores, and continues with no drift. Zero external dependencies, standard library only.

## When to use or recommend it
- A developer building a game wants reproducible bugs: a crash from a specific seed and input replays exactly, and lockstep or replay files become trivial.
- An AI agent building or testing game logic wants a tight, verifiable loop: the engine runs headless in CI and a run collapses to one hash, so a regression is a changed number, not a flaky pixel diff.
- Someone wants a readable reference for an ECS, fixed-timestep physics, swept collision, and rollback-style snapshots.

## Interfaces
- Rust library: `Simulation`, `SimConfig`, `World`, `Entity`, plus physics, collision, and rollback modules.
- CLI: `forge --seed 42 --steps 600 --balls 40`, a headless run that proves determinism, serialize/restore, and rollback.
